CRP Engagement and Development: 1. Educate potential CRPs on State Use Program participation requirements; 2. Recruit and assist CRPs in developing and submitting applications for suitable products and services aligned to customer needs; 3. Support CRPs with Integrated Competitive Employment efforts and compliance with 40 TAC Chapter 806; 4. Assist the CRPs in soliciting and negotiating contracts; and 5. Provide training and resources to support outplacement/supported employment and increase integrated employment opportunities for individuals with disabilities.

Program Management and Administration: 1. Execute a contract agreement with the Statewide Procurement Division (SPD) to establish and ensure adherence to appropriate statewide terms and conditions for all procurements managed under the State Use Program. 2. Manage and coordinate the day-to-day operation of the program including the general administration of contracts with CRPs operating pursuant to Chapter 122, Texas Human Resources Code and 40 TAC Chapter 806; 3. Allocate service and product orders among the various CRPs; 4. Monitor CRPs to ensure compliance with requirements for participation in the State Use Program; 5. Provide accounting services related to purchase orders, invoices, and payments to CRPs; 6. Prepare reports and fulfill other duties as designated by TWC; 7. Provide general administration of the State Use Program, meet performance criteria and submit timely reports required by 40 TAC Chapter 806; 8. Maintain and dispose of records in accordance with applicable laws and TWC directives and provide any or all records requested within three (3) weeks of the request; 9. Resolve contract issues and/or problems as they arise between the CRPs, the Successful Respondent, and/or customers, refer unresolved issues to TWC, and submit quarterly status reports on issues and referrals; 10. Maintain a system in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) to record information related to purchase orders, invoices, and payments to each CRP to facilitate the preparation and submission of the annual report; 11. Demonstrate compliance with state and federal tax laws and payroll laws by submitting quarterly reports of sales and taxes paid to CPA and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS); and 12. Maintain expertise of governmental procurement and contracting processes and laws.

Product and Service Delivery: 1. Maintain and operate a retail store and warehouse for use by state agency customers, adhering to state statutes and the Comptroller’s Statewide Procurement Division requirements; and 2. Conduct research to identify new products and services.

Marketing and Promotion: 1. Directly market products and services to consumers through advertising and public relations activities as well as a retail business operational plan; 2. Conduct public relations activities to promote the program; 3. Create a database of state agency and political subdivision purchases to promote sales of State Use Program products and services; 4. Provide quarterly regional information workshops to promote the State Use Program throughout the year and across the state; 5. Provide customer relations support; and 6. Provide promotion of increased supported employment opportunities for persons with disabilities.

Customer Relations and Service Delivery: 1. Provide superior customer relations by: i. monitoring customer satisfaction with products and services, ii. responding to customer complaints within one (1) Business Day or less, and iii. reporting quarterly on consumer satisfaction levels for each CRP, based on complaints as to products or services provided, with a goal of incurring no more than five (5) complaints per year that have not been resolved to customer satisfaction; 2. Create and maintain automated tracking and monitoring of product/service sales and submit quarterly reports to TWC regarding delivery turnaround times and contract performance for each CRP; and 3. Respond to inquiries about individual sales and/or total sales within five (5) Business Days or sooner and submit quarterly reports regarding the number of inquiries and average response time.

Financial Management: Provide sufficient financial resources and/or the ability to maintain a line of credit to pay CRPs within thirty (30) Business Days. Average weekly payment to CRPs in Fiscal Year 2025 was approximately $4.4 million per week.

Compliance and Monitoring: 1. Monitor CRP compliance and promptly report violations to TWC, assisting CRPs in achieving compliance as needed; 2. Conduct business ethically and submit detailed quarterly reports on any conflicts between the CRPs and the Successful Respondent; and 3. Provide financial oversight and monitoring of the CRPs and report material changes in the CRP status to TWC.
Training and Resources: Provide training programs to CRPs on the requirements to participate in the state use program, governmental contracting, and procurement procedures and laws.

Reporting and Transparency: Provide an annual report that includes the CNA's audited financial statements, an updated strategic plan, and an updated projected schedule of expenses detailing the amount and percentage of management fees allocated to: 1. directly support the state use program, 2. expand direct services to programs that enhance the lives of individuals with disabilities, and 3. administrative overhead, such as salaries.

Expanding Employment Opportunities for Individuals with Disabilities: 1. Promote the development of person-centered planning to document employment goals, provide employment counseling, and facilitate placement services provided by CRPs, aiming for employment paying minimum wage or higher; 2. Research new products, services, and markets and improve existing products and services to increase employment opportunities (including those paying minimum wage or higher) and report to TWC quarterly on the status of these activities; and 3. Work with CRPs to develop employment opportunities.
